C4H10 + Br2 → C4H9Br + HBr (UV light)

Homolytic fission: a covalent bond breaks so that each atom takes one electron from the shared pair, forming two radicals.

Free radical: Br• (or C4H9•).

(i) C4H10 + Br2 → C4H9Br + HBr (needs UV light), e.g. product CH3CH2CH2CH2Br or CH3CHBrCH2CH3.

(ii) Homolytic fission. The species that attacks butane is the bromine free radical, Br•.
Reagent: bromine, Br2. Condition: UV light (or sunlight, hf). The UV light splits Br2 into radicals.

Initiation: Br2 → 2Br• (homolytic fission by UV light).

Propagation: Br• + RCH3 → •CH2R + HBr; then •CH2R + Br2 → RCH2Br + Br•.

Termination (any one): Br• + Br• → Br2; RCH2• + Br• → RCH2Br; 2RCH2• → RCH2CH2R.

Propagation regenerates the radical, which makes it a chain reaction.

Initiation: Cl2 → 2Cl•
Essential condition: UV light (sunlight) – homolytic fission.
Propagation: Cl• + R–H → HCl + R• (and R• + Cl2 → RCl + Cl•).
Termination: Cl• + Cl• → Cl2 (or R• + Cl• → RCl, R• + R• → R–R).

(i) UV light/sunlight (or very high temperature), to cause homolytic fission of Br2.

(ii) Free-radical substitution is random: further/multiple substitution and substitution at other C atoms give a mixture of many products.
CH₄ + Br₂ → CH₃Br + HBr (with UV light)

(i) Initiation (UV light or high temperature must be stated): Br₂ → 2Br•
Propagation: Br• + CH₄ → •CH₃ + HBr; •CH₃ + Br₂ → CH₃Br + Br•
Termination (any one): Br• + Br• → Br₂; •CH₃ + Br• → CH₃Br; •CH₃ + •CH₃ → C₂H₆
Stages must be labelled to get full marks.

(ii) Methanol, CH₃OH, formed by nucleophilic substitution.

Initiation (UV light or high temperature): Br₂ → 2Br• (homolytic fission)

Propagation: Br• + C₂H₆ → •C₂H₅ + HBr; •C₂H₅ + Br₂ → C₂H₅Br + Br•

Termination (any one): Br• + Br• → Br₂; •C₂H₅ + Br• → C₂H₅Br; •C₂H₅ + •C₂H₅ → C₄H₁₀

Any mechanism with ions scores 0. Unlabelled stages score at most 3.

Initiation (UV light or heat): Cl₂ → 2Cl•

Propagation: Cl• + C₂H₆ → •C₂H₅ + HCl; •C₂H₅ + Cl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + Cl•

Termination (any one): Cl• + Cl• → Cl₂; •C₂H₅ + Cl• → C₂H₅Cl; 2 •C₂H₅ → C₄H₁₀

Unlabelled stages score at most 3.

(i) C3H8 + Br2 → C3H7Br + HBr. Condition: UV light (or high temperature); “reflux” is not accepted.

(ii) C3H6 + Br2 → C3H6Br2 (1,2-dibromopropane).

(iii) Propane: (free-radical) substitution. Propene: (electrophilic) addition.
Type: substitution. Mechanism: free-radical (chain) substitution. Both are needed for the mark.

(i) Propagation: C2H6 + •Cl → •C2H5 + HCl; then •C2H5 + Cl2 → C2H5Cl + •Cl. Termination (any one): •Cl + •Cl → Cl2; •C2H5 + •Cl → C2H5Cl; or 2•C2H5 → C4H10.

(ii) CH3CH2Cl: triplet (CH3, next to CH2) and quartet (CH2, next to CH3).

(iii) Any two of: its signal lies outside the range of most chemical shifts; it gives a single strong singlet (12 equivalent H); it is inert and volatile, so it is easily removed.

NO• + O3 → NO2• + O2

NO2• + O• → NO• + O2

NO is regenerated, so it acts as a catalyst. Overall: O3 + O• → 2O2.

Less ozone lets more UV radiation reach the Earth's surface. UV causes skin cancer, cataracts and tissue/DNA damage. Ozone loss is an international issue because the atmosphere is shared and the damage is not limited to the polluting country.

Initiation (UV light, homolytic fission): Cl2 → 2Cl•.

Propagation: Cl• + CH4 → HCl + •CH3, then •CH3 + Cl2 → CH3Cl + Cl•.

Show the radical dots. Cl• + CH4 → CH3Cl + H• is not accepted.

Initiation: Br2 → 2Br• (UV light/hν)

Propagation: Br• + C2H6 → C2H5• + HBr
C2H5• + Br2 → C2H5Br + Br•

Termination (any one): Br• + Br• → Br2; C2H5• + Br• → C2H5Br; C2H5• + C2H5• → C4H10

Propagation regenerates a radical, creating a chain reaction.

(i) Initiation: Br2 → 2Br• (homolytic fission), using UV light/sunlight (or high temperature).

(ii) Substitution on a methyl group: 4-methylbenzyl bromide, CH3C6H4CH2Br (one CH3 becomes CH2Br, ring and other CH3 unchanged) and HBr.

(i) Stratospheric ozone absorbs harmful UV radiation, protecting life on Earth.

(ii) NO(g) + O3(g) → NO2(g) + O2(g)
NO2(g) + O(g) → NO(g) + O2(g) (or NO2 + O3 → NO + 2O2). NO is regenerated, so it acts as a catalyst.

•NO + O3 → •NO2 + O2

•NO2 + •O → •NO + O2 (or •NO2 + O3 → •NO + 2O2)

Overall O3 + •O → 2O2; NO is regenerated, so it acts as a catalyst (one radical can destroy many ozone molecules).
